15596-bressant-a-novel.title: A Novel
15596-bressant-a-novel.creator: Julian Hawthorne
15596-bressant-a-novel.description: A book by Julian Hawthorne. in the house were open, and most of the windows, so that any one passing in the road might have looked up through the gabled porch and the passage-way, which divided the house, so to speak, into two parts, and seen the professor's brown-linen legs, and slippers down at the heel, projecting into view beyond the framework of the balcony-door.

arxiv-2101-03496.title: On a fractional reaction-diffusion models arising in population dynamics
arxiv-2101-03496.creator: S.H. Rasouli
arxiv-2101-03496.description: Abstract Abstract This paper is concerned with the existence of positive solutions for a fractional population model with the homogeneous Dirichlet condition on the exterior of a bounded domain. The approach is based on the sub-super solutions method. Our results generalize some recent results in the literature. Keywords: Fractional reaction-diffusion equation; Sub-supersolutions; Population models. AMS Subject Classification: 35J60, 35J61, 35R11.

arxiv-2202-04321.title: Optimal Congestion Control for Time-Varying Wireless Links
arxiv-2202-04321.creator: Prateesh Goyal, Mohammad Alizadeh, Thomas E. Anderson
arxiv-2202-04321.description: Abstract . Modern networks exhibit a high degree of variability in link rates. Cellular network bandwidth inherently varies with receiver motion and orientation, while class-based packet scheduling in datacenter and service provider networks induces high variability in available capacity for network tenants.

arxiv-2206-10500.title: A survey on association schemes on triples
arxiv-2206-10500.creator: Jose Maria P. Balmaceda, Dom Vito A. Briones
arxiv-2206-10500.description: Abstract . Association schemes on triples (ASTs) are ternary analogues of classical association schemes, whose relations and adjacency algebras are ternary instead of binary. We provide a survey of the current progress in the study of ASTs, highlighting open questions, suggesting research directions, and producing some related results.

arxiv-2305-17136.title: A simple approach to nonlinear nonholonomic systems with several examples
arxiv-2305-17136.creator: F. Talamucci
arxiv-2305-17136.description: Abstract The main theme of the article is the study of discrete systems of material points subjected to constraints not only of a geometric type (holonomic constraints) but also of a kinematic type (nonholonomic constraints). The setting up of the equations of motion follows a simple principle which generalizes the holonomic case.

arxiv-2306-03066.title: Accepted manuscript version of the paper published in IJCV 2024 (DOI: 10.1007/s11263-024-02118-3 ) Of Mice and Mates: Automated Classification and Modelling of Mouse Behaviour in Groups using a Single Model across Cages
arxiv-2306-03066.creator: Michael P. J. Camilleri, Rasneer S. Bains, Christopher K. I. Williams
arxiv-2306-03066.description: Abstract Behavioural experiments often happen in specialised arenas, but this may confound the analysis. To address this issue, we provide tools to study mice in the home-cage environment, equipping biologists with the possibility to capture the temporal aspect of the individual’s behaviour and model the interaction and interdependence between cage-mates with minimal human intervention.

arxiv-2309-11448.title: Reducing hardware requirements for entanglement distribution via joint hardware-protocol optimization
arxiv-2309-11448.creator: Adrià Labay Mora, Francisco Ferreira da Silva, Stephanie Wehner
arxiv-2309-11448.description: Abstract We conduct a numerical investigation of fiber-based entanglement distribution over distances of up to 1600 km 1600\text{\,}\mathrm{k}\mathrm{m} using a chain of processing-node quantum repeaters. We determine minimal hardware requirements while simultaneously optimizing over protocols for entanglement generation and entanglement purification, as well as over strategies for entanglement swapping.

arxiv-2405-13926.title: Some models are useful, but when?: A decision-theoretic approach to choosing when to refit large-scale prediction models Thanks: This work was supported in part by NIH/NIGMS R35 GM144128 and the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center J. Orin Edson Foundation Endowed Chair (SS and JTL), NIH/NIMH DP2 MH12 Than
arxiv-2405-13926.creator: Kentaro Hoffman
arxiv-2405-13926.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kentaro Hoffman. Large-scale prediction models using tools from artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning (ML) are increasingly common across a variety of industries and scientific domains. Despite their effectiveness, training AI and ML tools at scale can cost tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars (or more); and even after a model is trained, substantial resources must be invested to keep models up-to-date.

arxiv-2406-11963.title: Lepton Collider as a window to Reheating
arxiv-2406-11963.creator: Basabendu Barman, Subhaditya Bhattacharya, Sahabub Jahedi, Dipankar Pradhan, Abhik Sarkar
arxiv-2406-11963.description: Abstract We propose a search strategy for MeV-scale feebly interacting massive particle (FIMP) dark matter (DM) at the e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} collider. We argue, detection of a mono- γ \gamma signal plus missing energy can indicate to an MeV-scale reheating temperature of the Universe, after addressing observed DM abundance and other relevant constraints.

arxiv-2407-15306.title: Distribution of the zeros of polynomials near the unit circle
arxiv-2407-15306.creator: Mithun Kumar Das
arxiv-2407-15306.description: Abstract . We estimate the number of zeros of a polynomial in ℂ ⁡ [ z ] \mathbb{C}[z] within any small circular disc centered on the unit circle, which improves and comprehensively extends a result established by Borwein, Erdélyi, and Littmann [ 4 ] in 2008.

arxiv-2507-00653.title: Cognitive Load-Aware Inference: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Optimizing the Token Economy of Large Language Models
arxiv-2507-00653.creator: Yilun Zhang
arxiv-2507-00653.description: Abstract The escalating computational costs of Large Language Model (LLM) inference have become a critical barrier to their widespread and sustainable deployment. While existing optimization strategies are effective, they are predominantly based on statistical heuristics or architectural modifications, lacking a guiding cognitive theory to manage the inference process itself.

arxiv-2508-15696.title: C 1 C^{1} Smoothness of the Conjugacy in a Delayed Nonautonomous Hartman–Grobman Theorem via μ \mu -Dichotomies Thanks: This research has been supported by Agency for Research and Development, ANID-Chile through the grants ANID/FONDECYT 1240361 (Á. Castañeda) and the FONDECYT Postdoctorado project 3
arxiv-2508-15696.creator: Álvaro Castañeda, Heli Elorreaga
arxiv-2508-15696.description: Abstract . We investigate the differentiability of the conjugacy in a nonautonomous version of the Hartman–Grobman Theorem for systems with finite delay, where the linear part satisfies a μ \mu -dichotomy. Under suitable conditions on the nonlinear perturbation, the conjugacy is shown to be a C 1 C^{1} diffeomorphism. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 34D09,34k27,34k20,34k06 1.

arxiv-2509-00772.title: Flow Matters: Directional and Expressive GNNs for Heterophilic Graphs
arxiv-2509-00772.creator: Arman Gupta, Govind Waghmare, Gaurav Oberoi, Nitish Srivastava
arxiv-2509-00772.description: Abstract . In heterophilic graphs, where neighboring nodes often belong to different classes, conventional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) struggle due to their reliance on local homophilous neighborhoods. Prior studies suggest that modeling edge directionality in such graphs can increase effective homophily and improve classification performance. Simultaneously, recent work on polynomially expressive GNNs shows promise in capturing higher-order interactions among features.

arxiv-2509-14751.title: Probing initial isocurvature perturbation with 21cm one-point statistics
arxiv-2509-14751.creator: Zhenfei Qin, Hayato Shimabukuro
arxiv-2509-14751.description: Abstract Isocurvature perturbations—expected from multi-field inflation models—can leave unique signatures in the early Universe, but remain weakly constrained, especially on small scales. In this work, we investigate the constraining power of one-point statistics (variance and skewness) of the 21cm brightness temperature during Cosmic Dawn and the Epoch of Reionization, using semi-numerical simulations from 21cmFAST.

arxiv-2601-03451.title: Microeconomic Foundations of Multi-Agent Learning
arxiv-2601-03451.creator: Nassim Helou
arxiv-2601-03451.description: Abstract Modern AI systems increasingly operate inside markets and institutions where data, behavior, and incentives are endogenous. This paper develops an economic foundation for multi-agent learning by studying a principal–agent interaction in a Markov decision process with strategic externalities, where both the principal and the agent learn over time.

pmc-11372412.title: Bevacizumab Alone Versus Bevacizumab Plus Irinotecan in Patients With Recurrent Glioblastoma: A Nationwide Population-Based Study
pmc-11372412.creator: Yeonhu Lee, Eunyoung Lee, Tae Hoon Roh, Se-Hyuk Kim
pmc-11372412.description: BackgroundFor treating recurrent glioblastoma, for which there is no established treatment, the antiangiogenic antibody, bevacizumab, is used alone or with irinotecan. This study was aimed at comparing the survival of patients with recurrent glioblastoma receiving bevacizumab monotherapy and those receiving bevacizumab plus irinotecan combination therapy (B+I) by using a nationwide population-based dataset.MethodsPatients matching the International Classification of Diseases code C71.

pmc-11405727.title: The Ratio of A400/A1800 Mapping Identifies Chromosomal Regions Containing Known Photoprotection Recovery-Related Genes in Rice

The plant remains in photoprotection mode even after light intensity becomes not stressful for an extended period.

pmc-12584324.title: Forecasting COVID-19 inpatient mortality using fundamental parameters in resource-constrained settings: a countrywide multi-center cohort study
pmc-12584324.creator: Ibrahem Hanafi, Marah Alsalkini, Alaa Almouhammad, Ghaya Salhab, Qamar Khoder, Taj Azzam, Bayan Hanafi, Sondos Sallam, Majd Abu Khamis, Ola Alnabelsi, Lyana Alzamel, Zen Afif, Manaf Jassem, Rahaf Alsoudi, Samaher Almousa
pmc-12584324.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAccurate mortality prediction was essential for guiding hospitalization and management during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in low-resource settings with already fragile health systems. In such regions, political instability and weakened healthcare infrastructure amplified viral spread while constraining response capacity. Hospitalization was, therefore, mostly restricted to the most critical cases due to shortages of beds, staff, and equipment, leaving frontline physicians to make rapid triage decisions under pressure. Yet, most existing prognostic tools were unsuitable for use in such resource-constrained contexts.

pmc-12966786.title: Early experience with a composite ovine forestomach matrix graft in chronic lower extremity wounds: a multi-center retrospective case series
pmc-12966786.creator: James E Geiger, Anthony J LaLama, Alpash K Patel
pmc-12966786.description: Chronic wounds place a significant burden on patients and healthcare. A newer outpatient treatment is a composite bioscaffold that contains ovine forestomach matrix and hyaluronic acid (OFM-HA). This multi-center retrospective case series investigated OFM-HA in the treatment of lower extremity chronic wounds. Medical records of 10 patients were reviewed and patient and wound characteristics were documented.

pmc-12982353.title: A high-throughput screening platform for acetylcholinesterase inhibitors using a genetically encoded acetylcholine fluorescent sensor
pmc-12982353.creator: Xinxin Li, Yueming Yu, Siyu Li, Xueyang Lin, Chen Yang, Yufeng Yang, Shengran Wang, Mengwei Zhou, Zhenghao Bao, Xin Sui, Wenya Feng, Jun Yang, Daiying Zuo, Yuan Luo, Yongan Wang, Xianli Du
pmc-12982353.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) is a crucial hydrolytic enzyme in the central nervous system, responsible for the rapid degradation of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine (ACh) in the synaptic cleft, thereby maintaining the balance between neuronal excitation and inhibition. AChE is not only the primary target of neurotoxic agents and organophosphorus pesticides but its aberrant activity is also closely associated with various neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and myasthenia gravis.

pmc-12989547.title: MEDAI-LLM-SUMM: a reporting checklist for medical text summarization studies using large language models
pmc-12989547.creator: Anna N. Khoruzhaya, Mariya D. Varyukhina, Rustam A. Erizhokov, Ivan A. Blokhin, Roman V. Reshetnikov, Mariya R. Kodenko, Anastasia P. Pamova, Tikhon A. Burtsev, Kirill M. Arzamasov, Olga V. Omelyanskaya, Anton V. Vladzymyrskyy, Yuriy A. Vasilev
pmc-12989547.description: BackgroundMedical text summarization using large language models (LLMs) has reached an inflection point in 2024–2025, with adapted models demonstrating capability to match or exceed human expert performance in specific tasks. However, critical gaps persist in safety validation, evaluation frameworks, and clinical deployment readiness.

pmc-12990813.title: Dynapenic Abdominal Obesity and the Risk of Stroke in Postmenopausal Women
pmc-12990813.creator: Mingying Cao, Yan Zhang, Zhuhua Yao
pmc-12990813.description: BackgroundStroke is highly prevalent among middle-aged and older adults, posing a significant global health burden. Dynapenic abdominal obesity (DAO), a clinical phenotype integrating dynapenia and abdominal obesity, has been linked to various chronic diseases. However, its association with incident stroke in postmenopausal women remains unexplored.
